page_title: MemStats: Free RAM Monitor for the Mac Menu Bar

sources.entry: MemStats - Menu bar memory monitor that splits RAM usage by user account, groups helper processes into apps, and shows memory pressure and swap. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/sown-oss/MemStats) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.name: MemStats
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source macOS menu bar memory monitor that splits RAM use by user account and groups helper processes under their parent apps.
use_cases: see which user account is using RAM on a shared Mac
find which app is consuming memory
watch memory pressure and swap from the menu bar
spot a possible memory leak early
quit or force quit memory-hungry apps and processes
monitor RAM on a lab or build machine
summary.what_it_does: MemStats is a macOS menu bar app that shows RAM usage in a donut chart split by user account, with free memory and an unattributed slice so the numbers add up. It ranks apps by memory and rolls helper processes (such as Chrome or Slack helpers) up under the parent app, with list or treemap views. The menu bar title changes color with memory pressure, and swap is shown beside it. A short history (about two minutes at a glance, roughly ten minutes scrollable) is kept in memory only, and the app can flag steadily climbing or sudden jumps in a user's memory. Right-clicking an app or process offers quit, force quit, or copy PID, with quit limited to the user's own processes.
notable: Splits RAM usage by user account, useful on shared Macs
Groups helper processes under their parent apps
Open source with source code on GitHub
Makes zero network requests and keeps history only in memory
caveats: Requires macOS 14 Sonoma or later; supports Apple Silicon and Intel
Not distributed via the Mac App Store because the App Sandbox must be off; build is ad hoc signed and not yet notarized, so Gatekeeper requires manual approval
Does not monitor CPU, GPU, temperature, fans, network or weather; memory only
No automatic updates; process memory values from top may differ from other tools
